_note: Copy for The Bowery Gazette. Each list is a set of variants; the writer picks one deterministically per edition and item. Placeholders: {name} full name with title, {surname}, {given}, {occupation}, {street}, {age}, {weekday}, {product}, {bottles}, {price}, {verdict}, {coroner}, {months}, {pronoun} he/she, {object} him/her, {possessive} his/her, {ailment}, {cash}. Punch up: the joke is on the seller and the trade, never on the dead.

masthead.title: THE BOWERY GAZETTE
masthead.motto: The Leading Sensational, Sporting & Medical Journal of America
masthead.priceNote: Sold by All Newsdealers, Barbers & Druggists.

1: Bitter cold. Consumptives advised to lay in a supply.
5: Fair. Melancholy general among the unemployed.
6: Hot. Nerves frayed in the tenements.
9: Cooler. Catarrh returns with the children to school.
10: Damp. Neuralgia reported in Hester Street.
12: Snow. Goodwill toward men, and toward the trade.
Bitter. A good month for tonics.

{surname}.—Suddenly, at {possessive} residence in {street}, {name}, {occupation}, aged {age} years. {pronounCap} had been in excellent spirits.
{surname}.—Peacefully, {name}, {occupation}, aged {age} years. {pronounCap} slept soundly to the last.
{surname}.—{name}, {occupation}, of {street}, aged {age} years, after a short and remarkably cheerful illness.
{surname}.—On {weekday}, {name}, {occupation}, aged {age} years. Friends are respectfully invited. Boston papers please copy.

{surname}.—Infant child of {name}, aged {months} months. The family ask for privacy.

UNKNOWN.—The body of {someone}, name unknown, was found in a lodging-house in {street}. The keeper had not seen the lodger for some days, and had thought it a blessing.

Coroner {coroner} sat upon the death of {name}. A bottle found at the bedside was examined and pronounced "perfectly harmless, in moderation." Verdict: "{verdict}."

Coroner {coroner}, lately seen in a new overcoat, found that {name} "{verdict}." The jury was not consulted.

Coroner {coroner} found that {name} "{verdict}." The bottle at the bedside bore the label of {product}. The papers have been sent to the District Attorney.

Among the new customers at the shop this month: {name}, {occupation}, who complains of {ailment}.
{name}, {occupation}, of {street}, has tried every remedy for {ailment} but one, and as of this month has tried that one too.

{name}, of {street}, is in mourning, and has no further need of the remedy.

stockSeized: SEIZED.—Officers of the Board of Health carried away {bottles} bottles of {product} from the shop on Mulberry street.
adsLapsed: TO ADVERTISERS.—The notice of the proprietor of {product} could not be paid for at press, and does not appear in this edition. The Gazette prints on cash terms, like the coroner.

firstEdition.headline: A NEW CONCERN
decks: A PROPRIETOR OF REMEDIES OPENS HIS DOORS TO THE AFFLICTED OF THE WARD.
firstEdition.body: A new apothecary has opened on Mulberry street, with one copper still, a shelf of drugs and a dozen regular callers. Its proprietor, who styles himself Dr. ——, informs our reporter that he intends to cure the neighborhood of everything, and that the details are a trade secret. The ward wishes him every success, and has its coughs ready.

bodies: {name}, {occupation}, had for years endured {ailment}. "I tried everything," {pronoun} informs our reporter, "until a friend pressed upon me a bottle of {product}. After the first spoonful I felt nothing whatever. After the second I felt magnificent." {pronounCap} now takes it daily. Sold at the shop on Mulberry street, {price} the bottle.—Adv.
"I cannot do without it," says {name} of {product}, and {possessive} neighbors confirm that {pronoun} has not tried. For {ailment} and all kindred complaints. {price} the bottle.—Adv.
readingNotice.fallbackBody: {product} is purely vegetable, contains nothing injurious, and is recommended for infants, invalids and the aged. Sold at the shop on Mulberry street, {price} the bottle.—Adv.

tradeSales: {product} moved {bottles} bottles at the shop this month, at {price} the bottle.
tradeNoSales: The shop on Mulberry street sold nothing of its own manufacture this month. Its proprietor was seen staring at the still.
tradeBooks: The proprietor's books close the month at {cash}.

rivals.head: DR. GRIMSBY'S GALVANIC BELT
rivals.body: Worn next the skin. A Current of Health through every Nerve! Sent on thirty days' trial.
rivals.fine: Wearers are requested not to stand in puddles.

rivals.head: MRS. PRUDENCE WHITTLE'S VEGETABLE COMPOUND
rivals.body: Write to Mrs. Whittle in strictest confidence. She answers every letter personally.
rivals.fine: Mrs. Whittle's correspondence continues brisk, notwithstanding her funeral in March.

rivals.head: MADAME DE LA ROSE'S ARSENICAL COMPLEXION WAFERS
rivals.body: A Skin of Alabaster! Perfectly Safe! Ladies of Fashion take three daily.
rivals.fine: Her complexion was the envy of all who attended the viewing.

rivals.head: PROF. AUGUSTUS BLOOM'S HAIR RESTORER
rivals.body: Rubbed on nightly, it raises hair on billiard balls. Testimonials from the Bald of Three Continents.
rivals.fine: Do not apply to the face.

rivals.head: PROFESSOR KLINE'S ELECTRIC LIVER PAD
rivals.body: Laid upon the liver, it draws out bile, gloom and torpor by magnetism alone. No medicine required.
rivals.fine: Not to be worn near the watch.

rivals.head: THE ANTI-FAT CORDIAL
rivals.body: Reduces the figure by a pound a day without diet or exercise. Twelve ladies of Brooklyn have vanished entirely.
rivals.fine: The proprietors are not responsible for vanished ladies.

rivals.head: DR. ST. JOHN'S CONSUMPTION CURE
rivals.body: Cures consumption in all its stages. Testimonials from every state in the Union, and several beyond it.
rivals.fine: Several of the testimonials were received posthumously.

undertaker.head: FOGG & SONS,
undertaker.body: Coffins in All Sizes, Ready Made. We Thank Our Friends in the Medicine Trade for Their Continued Patronage.

quotes: My cough has quite gone quiet.
classifieds: WANTED.—TESTIMONIALS from persons restored to health. Liberal terms. Must be able to sign name, or make mark. Box 13, this office.
WANTED.—A smart BOY to paste labels. Must not read. Apply at rear entrance after dark.
LOST.—A tall gentleman's tape measure, near Mulberry street. Finder need not return it; he has another.
TO LET.—Furnished room, lately vacated, Mott street. The previous tenant will not be returning.
WANTED.—A respectable widow to answer letters in another lady's name. Discretion essential.
FOR SALE.—A quantity of empty bottles, slightly used. Apply to Fogg & Sons.
WANTED.—A PHYSICIAN willing to endorse anything. Diploma not required, but helpful.
WANTED.—A NIGHT WATCHMAN for a laboratory. Must be a heavy sleeper. Board included.
FOUND.—A bottle, green, three-quarters empty, in Baxter street. The owner will not be needing it.
SITUATION WANTED.—By a clergyman, to endorse remedies. References from the families of satisfied customers.
TO LET.—A cellar, suitable for brewing, dry, discreet. No questions; no windows.
WANTED.—Empty bottles of any make, bought by the gross. No enquiry made as to the former contents.
NOTICE.—The Ladies' Temperance League meets Thursdays. Members are reminded that bitters are not liquor.
regularsIntro: AMONG THE CALLERS.—{name}, {occupation}, troubled by {ailment}, has been seen at the new shop.

bankrupt.headline: A PROPRIETOR FAILS
decks: THE SHOP ON MULBERRY STREET IS SOLD UP; THE STILL GOES FOR SCRAP.
He Is Said to Be Considering the Law.
bankrupt.body: The proprietor of {product} has failed, owing money to the wholesale druggist, the landlord and the Gazette. His stock was sold at auction for less than the price of the bottles. Asked for a statement, he said that the public had not been ready for him. The public declined to comment.

shut_down.headline: CLOSED BY ORDER
decks: INSPECTORS SEAL THE PREMISES OF THE PROPRIETOR OF {product_upper}.
A Crowd Gathers; Some Are Disappointed.
shut_down.body: Acting upon complaints from the ward, the coroner's findings and the evidence of its own chemist, the Board of Health has closed the shop on Mulberry street and carried away its stock. The proprietor was not present. A tall gentleman in a hat was seen leaving by the rear entrance with a ledger under his arm.

timeline_end.headline: THE LAW ARRIVES
decks: The Pure Food and Drug Act.
FROM THE FIRST OF JANUARY, EVERY BOTTLE MUST SAY WHAT IS IN IT.
timeline_end.body: The new federal law takes effect this week. Proprietors of remedies must now declare upon the label any alcohol, opium, morphine, cocaine, chloroform or cannabis their preparations contain. The proprietor of {product} told our reporter that he welcomed the measure, and has ordered a great many new labels.

bribed.headline: THE CORONER IS SATISFIED
bribed.cutline: A GENTLEMAN LEAVING THE CORONER'S OFFICE.
decks: THE CORONER RETURNS HIS VERDICT IN TIME FOR LUNCHEON; NO BOTTLE IS EXAMINED.
bodies: The inquest upon the body of {name} was over before the jury had taken their coats off. Coroner {coroner} pronounced himself satisfied, and was seen afterward at Delmonico's, satisfied again.
Asked why no bottle was examined at the inquest upon {name}, Coroner {coroner} replied that he did not hold with chemistry, and that his new overcoat was none of our business.

The Coroner settled the matter of {name} himself, the jury being told that their views were not required. One juror, asked what he made of the evidence, said that there had not been any, and that this had been explained to him.

arrears.headline: A SHOP IN ARREARS
arrears.cutline: THE PROPRIETOR.—Not at home to callers.
decks: THE PROPRIETOR OF {product_upper} IS FOUND TO OWE MORE THAN HE HAS.
bodies: The proprietor of {product} owes the landlord, the wholesaler and the Gazette, in that order of patience. He informs our reporter that the remedy is on the point of a great success, and asked to borrow the car fare home.
A gentleman from the wholesale house on Pearl street called at the shop twice this month and was twice told the proprietor was out. The proprietor was seen through the window, mixing.
The landlord of the shop on Mulberry street has begun to read the deaths column with a professional interest, as the only column in which his tenant's affairs improve.

again.headline: THE PROPRIETOR STILL IN ARREARS
decks: THE BOOKS OF {product_upper} DO NOT IMPROVE; THE LANDLORD IS LOSING PATIENCE.

dull.headline: TRADE DULL ON MULBERRY STREET
decks: ONLY {sold_upper} BOTTLES SOLD; THE PROPRIETOR BLAMES THE WEATHER.
bodies: The shop on Mulberry street had a slow month. The proprietor attributes it to the weather, the price of coal and the jealousy of the medical faculty. His customers attribute it to the remedy.
Our reporter spent an afternoon at the shop and saw three customers, one of whom wanted directions. The proprietor sold him a bottle anyway.
Trade in {product} is reported quiet. The proprietor has been seen studying the advertisements of his rivals with the expression of a man reading his own obituary.

again.headline: TRADE STILL DULL
decks: ANOTHER SLOW MONTH AT THE SHOP ON MULBERRY STREET; THE PROPRIETOR NOW BLAMES THE PAPERS.

nothing.headline: NOT A BOTTLE SOLD
decks: THE SHOP ON MULBERRY STREET OPENS EVERY DAY AND SELLS NOTHING.
bodies: The shop on Mulberry street kept its hours all month and did not sell a single bottle. The ward continues to cough, and appears to prefer it.
Not one bottle left the shop on Mulberry street this month. The proprietor tells our reporter that he is building anticipation.

again.headline: ANOTHER MONTH WITHOUT A SALE
decks: NOT A BOTTLE SOLD; THE PROPRIETOR INSISTS IT IS A MATTER OF TIME.

growing.headline: NEW FACES AT THE COUNTER
decks: {joined_upper} NEW CUSTOMERS CALL AT THE SHOP ON MULBERRY STREET.
bodies: Word of {product} is going round the ward faster than the ailments it treats. Among this month's new customers is {name}, {occupation}, who heard of it from a neighbor and has not been the same since.
{name} is the latest of the ward to take up {product}. {pronounCap} tells our reporter that {pronoun} cannot say exactly what it does, but that {pronoun} feels it doing it.

again.headline: MORE NEW FACES
decks: {joined_upper} MORE CUSTOMERS TAKE UP THE REMEDY; THE OLD ONES DO NOT LET GO.

losing.headline: CUSTOMERS DESERT A REMEDY
losing.cutline: A FORMER CUSTOMER.—From a stock likeness.
decks: {left_upper} REGULARS STOP CALLING AT THE SHOP ON MULBERRY STREET.
bodies: Several of the proprietor's regulars have stopped calling at the shop. Some have got better; some have found another bottle; the proprietor declines to say which he finds more insulting.
The shop on Mulberry street is losing custom. {name}, lately a regular, tells our reporter that {pronoun} has given up the remedy, and feels about the same, and is saving the money.

again.headline: THE WARD DRIFTS AWAY
decks: {left_upper} MORE REGULARS GONE; THE PROPRIETOR TAKES IT PERSONALLY.

brisk.headline: BRISK TRADE ON MULBERRY STREET
decks: {sold_upper} BOTTLES SOLD AT THE SHOP THIS MONTH; THE PROPRIETOR IS SATISFIED, AND SO, FOR NOW, IS THE WARD.
bodies: Customers were seen leaving the shop with brown paper parcels and returning, some days later, for more. Our reporter asked one of them what the remedy was for. "For everything," he said, and asked our reporter for a dime.
The proprietor of {product} reports a good month and has bought a new hat on the strength of it. The hat is said to be the healthiest thing in the shop.
Business is good at the shop on Mulberry street. {name}, a regular, tells our reporter that {pronoun} would not be without the remedy, and has not tried to be.
The proprietor is counting his takings, and has twice been heard to laugh. The ward, which has heard him laugh before, is keeping its children indoors.

again.headline: TRADE HOLDS UP ON MULBERRY STREET
decks: {sold_upper} BOTTLES SOLD AGAIN; THE PROPRIETOR BEGINS TO SPEAK OF A SECOND SHOP.

shortage.headline: THE SHELF BARE ON MULBERRY STREET
shortage.cutline: A BOTTLE.—Not to be had for love or money.
decks: EVERY BOTTLE OF {product_upper} SOLD BEFORE THE MONTH WAS OUT; THE WARD WAITS.
The Proprietor Cannot Brew Fast Enough.
bodies: Callers at the shop on Mulberry street were sent away empty-handed in the last days of the month, the shelf being bare. Several waited on the step in the hope of a fresh batch, and one, being told there was none, wept.
The proprietor of {product} has sold out. Our reporter found a short queue outside the shop and a notice in the window: "MORE TUESDAY." Nobody in the queue looked well enough to wait until Tuesday.
There was not a bottle of {product} to be had in the ward by the month's end. Druggists report customers asking for it by name, and taking something else, and complaining.

again.headline: STILL NO BOTTLES TO BE HAD
decks: THE SHELF ON MULBERRY STREET BARE A SECOND MONTH; THE WARD GROWS IMPATIENT.

record.headline: A RECORD MONTH ON MULBERRY STREET
decks: {sold_upper} BOTTLES SOLD, AND THE BOOKS WELL UP; THE PROPRIETOR ORDERS A NEW HAT.
bodies: The shop on Mulberry street has had its best month yet, and the proprietor his best hat. Asked the secret of his success, he said it was the purity of his preparations, and laughed for some time.
Trade in {product} has never been brisker. Our reporter counted the callers on a single afternoon and lost count at forty; the proprietor did not, and will not say what it came to.

dear.headline: TOO DEAR FOR THE WARD
dear.cutline: A CALLER WHO ASKED THE PRICE.
decks: {turned_upper} CALLERS ASKED WHAT THE REMEDY COST AND WENT AWAY; THE PROPRIETOR CALLS IT QUALITY.
bodies: At {price} the bottle, the remedy of Mulberry street is beyond a good part of the ward. Our reporter watched a laborer read the card in the window, count his change, and go home to his cough.

The proprietor of {product} has put up his price to {price}, and his callers have put down their hats and left. He informs our reporter that a remedy cheaply sold is cheaply regarded, and that he would rather sell one bottle to a gentleman than three to the ward.
Several callers at the shop this month asked the price of {product} and were told {price}. Most of them are said to have found that they felt better already.

again.headline: STILL TOO DEAR
decks: The Price Holds, and So Do the Pennies.
{turned_upper} MORE CALLERS TURNED AWAY BY THE PRICE; THE PROPRIETOR HOLDS FIRM.

infantLead: The family had been giving the child a soothing preparation for its teeth, on the advice of the label. The physician who attended declined to say more, except that the child had been very quiet.
The mother, who is a regular customer of a certain soothing syrup, informs the neighbors that the child slept through every night since Easter, and this last one also.
Neighbors say the infant was the best-behaved child in the house: it never cried. The bottle on the mantel, which promised as much, is said to have been nearly empty.
unknownLead: No one has come forward to claim the body. A bottle, green, was found in the coat, and nothing else of value; the proprietor of the remedy has not come forward either.
The body lay a day in the dead-house before anyone thought to look at the bottle in its pocket. It was a remedy of the neighborhood, and three parts empty.

unlockNotices.second_still: IN THE TRADE.—A second copper still was carried into the back of a shop on Mulberry street this month. The neighbors report that the smell has doubled.
unlockNotices.third_still: IN THE TRADE.—A third still has gone into the shop on Mulberry street. The back room is now spoken of locally as "the works," and the landlord as a fortunate man.
unlockNotices.percolator: IN THE TRADE.—The proprietor of {product} has bought a glass percolator, and is said to be getting a great deal more out of his drugs. So, it is said, are his customers.
unlockNotices.newspaper_ads: TO ADVERTISERS.—The Gazette is pleased to announce that the proprietor of {product} is now in a position to buy space in these columns, having both money and a satisfied customer. Rates on application.
unlockNotices.doctor_title: IN THE TRADE.—The proprietor of {product} is to be addressed henceforward as Doctor. He has a diploma to show it, and the ink on it is very nearly dry.
unlockNotices.coroner_fees: IN THE TRADE.—It is said in Centre street that Coroner {coroner} is a practical man, and that proprietors who call on him before the jury sits seldom regret it.
unlockNotices.quality_control: IN THE TRADE.—The proprietor of {product} has engaged an assistant to taste each batch before it is bottled. The position was advertised three times.
unlockNotices.larger_shop: IN THE TRADE.—The wall between the shop on Mulberry street and the cobbler's next door has been knocked through, making room for twenty more regulars. The landlord has put the rent up five dollars a month, and the cobbler is understood to have been consulted afterward.
unlockNotices.bulk_supplier: IN THE TRADE.—A drug importer on Pearl street has agreed to supply the proprietor of {product} at a discount. The importer asks no questions, and is asked none.

deathLead: Friends describe the deceased as a regular and devoted customer of a certain remedy, which had lately become indispensable to {object}. The proprietor sends his condolences, and reminds the ward that the remedy is purely vegetable.
The deceased had been taking a remedy of the neighborhood for some months, and was heard to say that {pronoun} had never felt better. The physician who signed the certificate did not ask what it was.
{pronounCap} was a familiar figure at the shop on Mulberry street, where {pronoun} was known as a customer who never missed a month. The proprietor speaks of {object} warmly, and in the past tense.

exposedLead.headline: THE CORONER'S ENVELOPE
exposedLead.cutline: A GENTLEMAN WHO PAID THE CORONER'S FEE.
decks: A Bought Verdict Comes to Light.
IT IS SAID THAT THE INQUEST UPON {who_upper} WAS SETTLED BEFORE THE JURY SAT.
The District Attorney Is Asked to Look Into It.
exposedLead.body: An envelope that passed between the shop on Mulberry street and Centre street has been talked of in the ward, and now in the papers. Coroner {coroner} declines to discuss it, and is understood to have spent it. The verdict stands; the proprietor's name, which the envelope was meant to keep out of it, does not.

standing: POLICE COURT.—Patrick Hagan, 40, was fined two dollars for being drunk on Mott street. He told the Justice he had taken nothing but a tonic, and named it. The Justice fined the tonic also.
SHIPPING.—Arrived, the steamer Wyoming, from Liverpool, with 612 steerage and three cases of a patent pill for the trade. Both were landed.
A CARD.—The undersigned begs to inform his friends that he is not the Dr. —— of Mulberry street, and has never been, and will thank the ward to stop asking him for it.
SPORTING.—At Harry Hill's on Saturday, a sparring exhibition, four rounds, for a purse of ten dollars. The loser was revived with a remedy and is said to be doing well.
LOST.—On the Bowery, a gentleman's umbrella with a horn handle. Also his health, which he believes he left at a druggist's. Reward for the umbrella.
THE WEATHER.—The Signal Service predicts fair and colder. Druggists report the colder part already selling well.
BOARDING.—A quiet front room for a single gentleman of regular habits. No cooking, no dogs, no remedies in the room.
THE ELEVATED.—The Third Avenue line reports eleven passengers asleep at the terminus on Sunday, a record. All were roused but two, who were thought to be resting.
SPORTING.—The pedestrian match at the Garden enters its fifth day. The leader attributes his endurance to cold water and a clear conscience, and is not expected to win.
A CARD.—Mrs. E. Dooley wishes to thank the neighbors for their kindness during her late husband's illness, and the druggist on the corner for his.
WANTED.—A strong boy to carry bottles. Must not drink from them. Apply at the back.
AMUSEMENTS.—At the Bowery Theatre, "The Poisoned Chalice," a drama in five acts. The management guarantees every death in it is a stage death.
FOUND.—In Chatham square, a purse containing forty cents and a recipe. The finder has kept the forty cents.

POLICE COURT.—A woman was charged with taking a bottle of soothing syrup from a counter in Hester street. The Justice, on learning the make of the syrup, discharged her and sent an officer for the proprietor.
THE HARBOR.—Two schooners in from Savannah with turpentine and rosin. The rosin is for the trade; the turpentine, it is said, is for the remedies.
CITY HALL.—The Aldermen met for eleven minutes and voted themselves a dinner. The question of the street-cleaning contract was referred to the dinner.
A CARD.—Prof. Lacour, the celebrated mesmerist, is obliged to postpone his lectures at Cooper Union, having been unable to wake his assistant.
THE SEASON.—Oysters are in, and so are the complaints. Physicians report a brisk trade in stomachs; druggists report the same.
SPORTING.—The Metropolitans beat the Brooklyns by eleven runs to four. The Atlantics' pitcher had taken a tonic for his arm.
LOST.—A pocketbook, in a Third Avenue car, containing a pawn ticket and a prescription. The prescription is of no value to the finder.
WANTED.—A lady of refinement to sign letters of thanks for a remedy. No experience of the remedy required.
TO LET.—Two rooms over a druggist's. The smell, the landlord says, is wholesome.
POLICE COURT.—A peddler of 'Vital Bitters' was fined for obstructing the sidewalk with a crowd. The Justice did not inquire into the bitters, and bought a bottle.
FIRE.—A blaze in a tenement in Baxter street was put out by the engine company before the third floor caught. A quantity of patent medicine in a rear room burned with a blue flame for an hour.
THE WEATHER.—Hot and close. The Health Department urges the poor to keep out of the sun, and the rich to keep out of the city, which they have.
AMUSEMENTS.—At the Bowery dime museum, the Living Skeleton is to wed the Fat Lady on Thursday. The bride attributes her figure to a remedy; the groom attributes his to another.
SHIPPING.—Cleared, the steamer Germanic for Liverpool, with grain, cotton and forty cases of an American remedy for the English market, which is said to be in need of it.
A CARD.—The undersigned has not been cured by any remedy whatever, and wishes it known, having been asked eleven times this week.
WANTED.—A man with a good beard to stand in a window and be pointed at. Apply to the proprietor of a hair restorer.
THE COURTS.—A suit by a customer against a proprietor of bitters, on the ground that they contained no bitters, was dismissed. The Judge found that nobody had expected them to.
FOUND.—On the steps of a church in Mott street, a basket containing a bottle of soothing syrup and nothing else. The police are inquiring for the rest.
STREET SCENE.—A sandwich man advertising a cure for consumption was taken ill at the corner of Canal street and carried home coughing, still advertising.
MARKETS.—Butter firm, eggs easier, coal dear. Patent medicines, as always, cheaper to make than to buy.
SPORTING.—At this office, a challenge: any man in the Sixth Ward may try the dumb-bells for a purse of five dollars. The purse has not been touched since Easter.
THE ELEVATED.—A gentleman fell asleep on the Second Avenue line and rode it six times. He is said to have been taking something for his nerves.
BOARDING.—Table board for gentlemen, two dollars a week. Medicines not provided at table.
CHARITY.—The ladies of St. Bartholomew's held a fair for the poor of the Sixth Ward. The poor were not admitted, but are said to have done well out of it.
WANTED.—Bottles, half-pint, round, green, by the gross. A good price for any that have been washed.
THE COURTS.—A druggist sued by a widow was found not liable, the jury holding that her husband had read the label and should have known better. The label said 'harmless.'

prospectHints.doctor_title: the title of Doctor, which the ward allows a man in good standing, and Cincinnati allows anyone with fifty dollars
prospectHints.third_still: a third copper, which the coppersmith keeps for a house that has sold a thousand bottles
prospectHints.coroner_fees: an understanding with the coroner, which every proprietor comes to after his first inquest
prospectHints.quality_control: a chemist of his own, to be engaged after forty batches with a hundred dollars put by, or at once if a bad batch ever comes to light
prospectHints.larger_shop: the cobbler's shop next door, which the landlord will let to a proprietor with twenty-five regulars and two hundred dollars
prospectHints.bulk_supplier: terms from an importer on Pearl street, who gives them to a house that has brewed twenty-five batches

standingDated.text: THE PEDESTAL FUND.—The World's subscription for the Statue's pedestal passes ninety thousand dollars. A proprietor of bitters has offered a hundred if the lady may hold one of his bottles instead of the torch.
GENERAL GRANT.—The ward is draped in black for the General's funeral. The druggists report that the General was a martyr to his throat, and that their throat lozenges are now for sale at a reduction.
THE STATUE.—Liberty is unveiled in the harbor in a fog so thick that the guns could not find her. The ward celebrated with fireworks and a remedy, and some will feel both for a week.
THE BLIZZARD.—Snow to the second story in Mulberry street; no cars, no coal, no milk. The druggists alone kept their doors open, and their prices.
THE BRIDGE.—Twenty thousand crossed the Brooklyn Bridge on Sunday. A hawker of a cure for vertigo did a good trade at the middle.
THE ELECTION.—The ward voted early and often. A remedy for hoarseness was given away at the polling place, by a candidate who had several.

verdictLead: The bottle found at the bedside bore the label of {label}. Whether its proprietor spoke for his preparations or kept away, it did not detain the jury long. Physicians observe that the remedy is purely vegetable, and that so is hemlock.

A chemist from the College of Pharmacy gave evidence that the bottle of {label} contained, besides syrup and spirit, enough of a certain drug to quiet a dray-horse. The proprietor's advertisements describe it as gentle.
The jury retired for twenty minutes and returned with the label of {label} written into its verdict. The foreman remarked that he had a bottle of it at home, and would be pouring it away.

investmentNotices.branch_shop.bought: IN THE TRADE.—The proprietor of {product} has taken a corner shop in the Ninth Ward, fitted with counter and gas, and put a clerk in it. The Ninth Ward is said to be delighted, and has not yet been asked.
investmentNotices.almanac.bought: IN THE TRADE.—Ten thousand copies of the proprietor's almanac are going about the city, with the moon's phases, a recipe for pickles and every claim on his label. The pickles are said to be reliable.
investmentNotices.wholesale_contract.bought: IN THE TRADE.—Messrs. Hegeman & Co. of Paterson will take the goods of {product} by the dozen, for druggists in Paterson, Newark and Yonkers. New Jersey is to be cured wholesale.
investmentNotices.laboratory.bought: IN THE TRADE.—A back room on Mulberry street has been fitted with retorts, and a German chemist installed who asks no questions. The neighbors have begun to ask some.
investmentNotices.almanac.lapsed: IN THE TRADE.—The proprietor's almanac for the year is out of date, and is now chiefly used for lighting fires. It may be had again on application.
investmentNotices.branch_shop.lost: IN THE TRADE.—The branch in the Ninth Ward has put up its shutters. The clerk is said to have taken the till, and the ward to have taken the clerk's side.
investmentNotices.wholesale_contract.lost: IN THE TRADE.—Messrs. Hegeman & Co. of Paterson have cancelled their order for {product}, having read the papers. New Jersey will have to find its own remedies.
investmentNotices.laboratory.mishap: FIRE.—A blaze in a back room on Mulberry street brought out Engine No. 9 on {weekday}. A quantity of ether was found to be the cause, and a German chemist the excuse. The proprietor's loss is put at twenty-five dollars, and the talk at a good deal more.

outOfTown: OUT OF TOWN.—A death at Paterson is laid by the family to a remedy bought from a druggist there. The druggist says he had it by the dozen from New-York, and is sorry.
OUT OF TOWN.—The Newark papers report a death from a patent medicine sold over a counter in Market street. The bottle came from New-York, by the gross.
OUT OF TOWN.—At Yonkers, a coroner's jury has found that a laborer died of a remedy he did not know the name of. Nor, it is said, did the druggist who sold it.
